answer: Spectral analysis at the orchard: each identity is a node, and the second eigenvalue of the trust graph bounds how easily a cluster can be cut. The summit of honest connectivity stays high because real operators link across diverse subgraphs. A falcon of collusion — dense internal edges, sparse external ones — spikes that eigenvalue and flags the cluster. Faking 1,000 identities with organic cross-links costs roughly 10,000 verified attestations, exceeding the reward pool, so the attacker's break-even never arrives.
